kaps_punt: Erfenis in die name van die plekke: Voorbeeld: Name van riviere, damme en dorpe: Vrystaat

items.bewering: Elke rivier, dam en dorp in die Vrystaat het 'n naam wat iemand gekies het.
items.bron: Place names are given by people: Encyclopedia.com 'place name' (https://www.encyclopedia.com/humanities/encyclopedias-almanacs-transcripts-and-maps/place-name); the lesson's own examples each have a documented namer (Gordon named the Oranje in 1779, SAHO dated event; J.N. Brits named his farm Bloemfontein, SAHO node 65347; the dam was renamed officially in 1996). Loose for names like Gariep that grew out of everyday speech rather than a single choice, but not false at this level.

items.bewering: So 'n pleknaam vertel watter mense in die gebied gewoon het en watter taal hulle gepraat het.
items.bron: Stated of every place name ('so 'n pleknaam' points back to 'elke rivier, dam en dorp'), and it fails on two of the lesson's own four examples. Oranjerivier was given in 1779 by Robert Jacob Gordon, a VOC officer on an expedition, in honour of Prince William V of Orange (SAHO dated event 'Orange River named in honour of Prince William V of Orange by Col. Robert Gordon', 17 Aug 1779; Wikipedia 'Orange River', citing Earle et al. 2005): it tells who named the river and whom they honoured, not who lived along it. Hendrik Verwoerd-dam was named after the prime minister (Wikipedia 'Gariep Dam'; Daily Maverick 20 Feb 2023): it tells who held power, not who lived in the area. The language of a name is the language of whoever gave it, who need not have lived there.
items.regstelling: Narrow the quantifier and attach the claim to the namer, not the residents: a place name KAN (of DIKWELS) vertel watter mense 'n plek benoem het en watter taal hulle gepraat het. Keep the next sentence (it also tells something of the area's history), which holds for all four examples.

items.bewering: Dit vertel ook iets van die gebied se geskiedenis.
items.bron: Holds for each example in the lesson: Gariep (pre-colonial Khoekhoe name, Wikipedia 'Orange River' citing Earle et al. 2005), Oranje (VOC naming 1779, SAHO), Verwoerd/Gariep dam (renamed after apartheid, Wikipedia 'Gariep Dam'; Daily Maverick 2023).

items.bewering: Name vertel 'n storie (opskrif; die beeld dat 'n naam 'n storie vertel en 'n deel van die geskiedenis 'dra')
items.bron: Mapping checked: a name carries evidence of who gave it, in what language and when, which is what the lesson then shows with Gariep, Oranje, Bloemfontein and the dam. Where a learner might push it too far (reading the residents' identity straight off any name) is the fault already reported in the item above; the image itself holds once that sentence is narrowed.

items.bewering: Die Oranjerivier is Suid-Afrika se langste rivier.
items.bron: Britannica 'Orange River' (https://www.britannica.com/place/Orange-River; snippet: 'The Orange River is the longest in South Africa'); Wikipedia 'Orange River' ('It is the longest river in South Africa', total length about 2 432 km citing Britannica). Lengths differ by source (about 2 090 to 2 432 km) but none disputes the ranking, and the lesson gives no length.

items.bewering: Lank voordat Europeërs hier aangekom het, het die Khoikhoi dit Gariep genoem.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Orange River', citing Earle et al. (2005) A preliminary basin profile of the Orange/Senqu River and Schoeman, Early White Travellers in the Transgariep: pre-colonial inhabitants called it Kai !Arib ('Great River'), from which the form Gariep derives. Gordon's 1779 manuscript records the Namaqua name 'Garie' (UCT iBali San and Khoen digital archive, item 20511, as reported in search results; the page itself was behind a browser check). Daily Maverick (20 Feb 2023) calls Gariep 'the original Khoi name for the river'. Note for the writer, not a fault: 'Gariep' is the Dutch/Afrikaans spelling of the Khoekhoe word (!Garib); at Grade 5 naming it Gariep is accurate enough.

items.bewering: Gariep is 'n inheemse naam uit die taal van die Khoikhoi.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Gariep Dam' (citing HSRC Dictionary of Southern African Place Names, p. 171): Gariep is a Khoekhoe word, the original name of the Orange River. Wikipedia 'Orange River': Khoekhoegowab !Garib rendered in Afrikaans as Gariep. Sources differ on the meaning ('river' versus 'great river'); the lesson does not state a meaning, so the difference does not touch it.

items.bewering: Die naam Oranjerivier het eers baie later met reisigers uit Europa gekom.
items.bron: SAHO dated event, 17 August 1779: the Orange River named in honour of Prince William V of Orange by Col. Robert Gordon. Wikipedia 'Orange River' (citing Earle et al. 2005): named by Robert Jacob Gordon on a trip to the interior in 1779. Earlier Dutch settlers called it Groote Rivier.

items.bewering: Elke naam dra 'n ander deel van die rivier se geskiedenis.
items.bron: Follows from the two verified namings: a pre-colonial Khoekhoe name and a 1779 VOC name (Wikipedia 'Orange River'; SAHO dated event 1779).

items.bewering: Bloemfontein is die hoofstad van die Vrystaat.
items.bron: SAHO 'Bloemfontein' (https://www.sahistory.org.za/place/bloemfontein): 'Bloemfontein is the capital City of the Free State Province'. Wikipedia 'Bloemfontein': capital and largest city of the Free State province.

items.bewering: Die naam het 'n Nederlandse oorsprong en bestaan uit die woorde vir blom en fontein.
items.bron: SAHO node 65347 (Bloemfontein history): trekboer J.N. Brits named his farm after the flowers (wild clover) round the spring, before Major Warden founded the village there in 1846. The name is the Dutch bloem + fontein (Afrikaans blom, fontein). On the minority account (after the Griqua/Korana leader Jan Bloem, Wikipedia 'Bloemfontein') the first part is a surname, but that surname is the same word, so the sentence still holds, and the next sentence covers the disagreement.

items.bewering: Daar is meer as een storie oor hoe die plek dié naam gekry het.
items.bron: SAHO node 65347 (flowers round Brits's spring); Wikipedia 'Bloemfontein' ('possible etymology... Bloem's fountain, after Jan Bloem II, a Griqua leader'); other accounts name a neighbour, Griesel, or an ox called Bloem taken by a lion. Several published accounts exist and none is settled.

items.bewering: Die Gariepdam lê op die Oranjerivier, op die grens tussen die Vrystaat en die Oos-Kaap.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Gariep Dam' ('bordering the Free State and Eastern Cape provinces', on the Orange River about 48 km north-east of Colesberg); Daily Maverick 20 Feb 2023 ('the invisible line dividing the Eastern Cape from the Free State'; it also notes the Northern Cape meets close by, which does not make the lesson's sentence wrong); SAHO dated event on the 'Hendrik Verwoerd Dam (now Gariep Dam) on the Orange'.

items.bewering: Eers was dit die Hendrik Verwoerd-dam.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Gariep Dam': originally named the Hendrik Verwoerd Dam when commissioned in 1971; SAHO dated event 'Hendrik Verwoerd Dam (now Gariep Dam)'; Encyclopaedia Philatelica catalogue note citing Raper (1987). Daily Maverick (2023) adds that the project was first called the Ruigte Valley Dam before being named after Verwoerd. That was a planning name before the dam opened. The Verwoerd name was the one it carried as a working dam until 1996, so 'eers' read against the 1996 renaming is correct.

items.bewering: Verwoerd was 'n eerste minister in die apartheidsjare.
items.bron: SAHO 'Hendrik Verwoerd becomes Prime Minister' (2 September 1958) and SAHO entry on his assassination (6 September 1966); Wikipedia 'Hendrik Verwoerd' (prime minister 1958-1966). 'Eerste minister' here is the office, not a superlative.

items.bewering: In 1996 is die dam hernoem tot die Gariepdam, met die rivier se ou Khoikhoi-naam.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Gariep Dam' ('officially changed to Gariep Dam on 4 October 1996'); Daily Maverick 20 Feb 2023 ('renamed the Gariep Dam in 1996'; 'the original Khoi name for the river'); Encyclopaedia Philatelica note citing Raper ('officially changed to Gariep Dam in 1996').

items.bewering: Die rivier het dieselfde gebly, maar die dam se naam het verander.
items.bron: The river's official name is still the Orange River (Wikipedia 'Orange River'; New World Encyclopedia 'Orange River': Gariep is favoured in some official correspondence while Orange keeps wider recognition). Only the dam was officially renamed in 1996 (Wikipedia 'Gariep Dam').

items.bewering: Name kan verander soos 'n land verander.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Gariep Dam': after the end of apartheid the Verwoerd name was considered unsuitable and was changed in 1996; Encyclopaedia Philatelica note citing Raper says the same.

items.bewering: 'n Nuwe naam vertel ook iets van wie ons vandag is.
items.bron: An interpretation rather than a factual claim. It fits the documented reason for the renaming: the apartheid-era name was judged unsuitable and was replaced with the pre-colonial Khoekhoe name (Wikipedia 'Gariep Dam'; Daily Maverick 2023).

items.bewering: pleknaam: Die naam van 'n plek, soos 'n rivier, 'n dam of 'n dorp.
items.bron: Encyclopedia.com 'place name' (a name used to identify a geographic locality such as a town, river or mountain); Dictionary.com 'toponym' ('the name of a place').

items.bewering: inheemse naam: 'n Naam uit die taal van mense wat al eeue lank in 'n gebied woon.
items.bron: Merriam-Webster 'Indigenous' (sense for peoples): 'of, relating to, or descended from the earliest known inhabitants of a place and especially of a place that was colonized'; it also notes that 'indigenous' applies to what has never been introduced or brought from elsewhere. Wiktionary 'inheems': native, indigenous, autochthonous, as opposed to 'uitheems'. The idea is origin in the place, not how long people have lived there. The lesson's definition rests only on length of stay. Dutch- and Afrikaans-speaking people have lived in the Free State since at least the 1820s and in South Africa since 1652, which is centuries, so by this entry 'Bloemfontein' (a Dutch name, per the lesson) and even 'Oranjerivier' would count as inheemse name. That contradicts the lesson's own contrast between the indigenous Gariep and the later European names. A glossary entry is read on its own, so the contradiction is not fixed by the surrounding blocks.
items.regstelling: Define it by origin and by who was there before the newcomers, not by length of stay: an inheemse naam is a name from the language of the people who lived in an area long before settlers came from other lands, or of the people whose language has its roots in that area. Avoid 'die eerste mense' as the definition: the Khoikhoi were not the first people at the Gariep (San hunter-gatherers were there before them), so that wording would create a new false claim.

items.bewering: hernoem: Om iets 'n nuwe naam te gee in plaas van sy ou naam.
items.bron: Standard sense of 'rename' (give a new name in place of the old one), Merriam-Webster 'rename'; the 1996 renaming of the dam fits it exactly (Wikipedia 'Gariep Dam').

items.bewering: apartheid: 'n Stelsel van wette wat mense in Suid-Afrika volgens ras geskei en ongelyk behandel het.
items.bron: SAHO 'Background and policy of apartheid' (https://www.sahistory.org.za/article/history-apartheid-south-Africa): the National Party's policy from 1948 made segregation law, with people classified by race (Population Registration Act 1950) and separated (Group Areas Act 1950), and it was carried out so that equal development was impossible. History.com 'Apartheid' says the same.

opsomming: Twee feite moet reggemaak word en die res is bevestig, ook die enigste oortreffende trap ('langste rivier') en die jaartal 1996. Eerstens sê die les dat 'n pleknaam vertel watter mense in die gebied gewoon het, maar dit is vals vir twee van sy eie voorbeelde: Oranjerivier en die Verwoerd-dam is gegee deur mense wat nie daar gewoon het nie. Die stelling moet 'kan' of 'dikwels' kry en oor die mense gaan wat die naam gegee het. Tweedens omskryf die begrip 'inheemse naam' die woord net met hoe lank mense al in 'n gebied woon. Dan tel Nederlandse name soos Bloemfontein ook as inheems, wat die les se eie kontras ondermyn.
